blocks.text: I can create a specific atmosphere by linking vocabulary choices and creating a semantic field.

items.title: Using adjectives and {semantic fields} to plan

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Describing something in an interesting and detailed way.
The feeling or sense evoked by the setting or environment.
A word that describes or defines a noun.
The act of deciding how to do something.
A group of words or expressions that are related in meaning.

blocks.text: Descriptive writing is designed to create a clear **atmosphere** for the reader and to paint a picture of an image.
You can build this skill so well that you can embed it in narrative writing, or even in a persuasive piece of writing, to create a specific effect on your audience.
A **semantic field** is a group of words or expressions that are related in meaning.
Using a semantic field helps us to create a consistent image for the reader. It is a pattern over the course of your text, made of words that are linked in their meaning.
If you can create a consistent image, you help the reader to soak into the atmosphere.
Choose your adjectives carefully in a descriptive paragraph in order to create a semantic field.
Imagine an image of an idyllic scene: a river, flowers, trees and a bright blue sky above. Four focal points can jump out at you.

items.title: Sky
items.sub: The blue sky and sunlight catching the flowers

items.title: River and bridge
items.sub: The clear water with the bridge running over it

slides.title: Decide the feeling, then choose adjectives

blocks.text: To create a semantic field, first decide what the overall feeling associated with the image is. Think about the colours, the weather above and the stillness of the water.

blocks.label: What overall feeling do you get?
blocks.text: You might feel a sense of **calmness and tranquillity** when you picture this scene.
Now choose adjectives that fit the overall mood of calmness and tranquillity, going beyond just ‘purple’ or ‘pink’.

slides.title: Do the words match the mood?

blocks.text: Why might adjectives such as ‘vibrant’, ‘kaleidoscopic’ and ‘ravishing’ not be as effective in this description?

blocks.label: Tap for the reason
blocks.text: These words give the impression of a scene that is more loud and overwhelmingly beautiful, rather than the calm, tranquil scene we are trying to describe.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: You should reach for ambitious words, but not just the most impressive-sounding ones. Make sure that all the words you use are creating a consistent atmosphere.
As well as describing the focal points, think about how you move through the scene. We want a sense of progression, and we want to glide through it rather than just have a static view.
Which words would add to a semantic field of calmness when moving through a scene?

slides.title: Does it fit a calm scene?

blocks.q: Sort the words: would you use them to create a calm semantic field?

blocks.text: To plan a paragraph, use a single paragraph outline with three parts.

items.title: Focus of the paragraph
items.sub: Which part of the image you will focus on, and what kind of language you might use

items.title: Supporting detail
items.sub: Notes on details, for example petal colour

items.title: Concluding idea
items.sub: The feeling you want to leave the reader with

blocks.label: Example outline: daisies
blocks.text: **Focus:** Daisies. Heavenly imagery, as if they are angels. **Supporting details:** petals are white, centres are golden; feelings of disbelief at their beauty; stems swaying in the wind; the scent is intoxicating, bewitching, captivating. **Concluding idea:** carrying that pure joy at the sight and smell of the flowers away with you.

blocks.label: Example outline: the sky
blocks.text: **Focus:** Clear sky. Feelings of calmness and tranquillity. **Supporting details:** colour = cerulean; eyes drifting towards the sky; serene; the sky is cloudless. **Concluding idea:** looking at the sky creates the feeling of a deep, calming exhale.
A strong concluding idea is impactful, so that it stays with the reader.

blocks.q: Match each part of the outline to what you write in it.

pairs.b: which part of the image, and what kind of language
notes on details, such as petal colour
the feeling you want to leave the reader with

blocks.text: A student wrote: ‘The tall trees towered above me and I could feel their weight pressing down on me. When the sunlight caught the bark, the dappled effect was like a calming ripple in the water.’

blocks.label: What feedback would you give?
blocks.text: The trees feel oppressive in their weight, but then also calming at the same time. This doesn’t create a clear image for the reader. Create a consistent mood throughout to help the reader imagine the scene.

blocks.label: How could it be fixed?
blocks.text: Continue the oppressive atmosphere in the second sentence instead of bringing in a calming picture: ‘The dappled effect was like a disease spreading amongst the trees.’
Here is a sentence that does create a semantic field: ‘The serene sky enveloped me in a comforting hug.’ The words ‘serene’, ‘enveloped’, ‘comforting’ and ‘hug’ all create a soothing tone.
It’s not about using the biggest words in your vocabulary. It’s about making sure the words come together effectively.

items.q: Which group of words makes a calm semantic field?
Why was the student’s paragraph about the trees confusing?
options: It mixed an oppressive mood with a calming one

items.q: Which of these would fit a semantic field of calmness?
The serene sky enveloped me in a comforting hug. What tone do these words create?

blocks.text: Now write your descriptive paragraphs from your plan. Remember to use adjectives and verbs to create a semantic field.
Then edit your work. Read back over it. Could you:

items: find more ambitious adjectives to describe the focal points of the image?
add more variety to the verbs in your descriptive paragraphs?
create a more consistent semantic field?
Descriptive writing is designed to create a clear atmosphere for the reader and paint a picture of an image.
Semantic fields can be used to create that picture for the reader.
A semantic field is a group of words or expressions that are related in meaning.
Choose your adjectives carefully in a descriptive paragraph in order to create a semantic field.

flashcards.front: Why is a semantic field effective in descriptive writing?
flashcards.back: It helps to create a consistent image for the reader.
The act of deciding how to do something.

flashcards.back: The overall feeling associated with the image (for example calmness and tranquillity).

flashcards.back: They give the impression of a scene that is more loud and overwhelmingly beautiful than calm and tranquil.

flashcards.back: Focus of the paragraph, supporting detail and concluding idea.

flashcards.back: The feeling you want to leave the reader with.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Using adjectives and semantic fields to plan and write descriptive paragraphs
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word or short phrase, using what you have learned about atmosphere, adjectives, semantic fields and planning a paragraph.

questions.prompt: What is the name for a group of words or expressions that are related in meaning?
questions.explanation: That is the definition of a semantic field.

questions.prompt: Which word means the feeling or sense evoked by the setting or environment?
questions.explanation: Atmosphere is the feeling or sense evoked by the setting or environment.

questions.prompt: What type of writing is designed to create a clear atmosphere and paint a picture for the reader?
questions.explanation: Descriptive writing is designed to create an atmosphere and paint a picture.
They are words that describe nouns such as the sky or the river.

questions.prompt: The lesson chose the overall mood of calmness and what? Answer with one word meaning peacefulness, starting with ‘t’.
questions.explanation: The lesson chooses calmness and tranquillity as the overall mood.

questions.prompt: Which word does NOT fit a calm scene: serene, placid, cacophonous or soothing?
questions.explanation: Serene, placid and soothing are calm words, but cacophonous is not helpful in describing a calm image.

questions.prompt: Which verb fits a calm scene: marching or strolling?
questions.explanation: Strolling is a leisurely movement that adds to a semantic field of calmness.

questions.prompt: In the single paragraph outline, which box do you use for the feeling you want to leave the reader with?
questions.explanation: The concluding idea is where you note the feeling you want to leave the reader with.

questions.prompt: In the single paragraph outline, which box do you use for notes on details such as petal colour?
questions.explanation: The supporting detail box lists notes on details.

questions.prompt: ‘Serene’, ‘enveloped’, ‘comforting’ and ‘hug’ create which tone: soothing or tense?
questions.explanation: All of these words feel calm and comforting, so they create a soothing tone.
